Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
1218 PM PST Thu Nov 26 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Mild temperatures with dry conditions nearly areawide through
  Sunday morning. 

* Low chances (20% or less) for light rain showers along the OR
  border Friday afternoon and evening. 

* Rain and high elevation snow returns Sunday into Tuesday, with 
  strong ridgetop gusts. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

Happy Thanksgiving, everyone! This forecaster hopes your
turkey and stuffing is anything but our current weekend forecast;
dry and mild. Highs will be in the 50s areawide through Saturday 
with cloudy skies. Fog-prone valleys across the Sierra may see 
freezing fog development each morning, though high cloud cover may
limit fog extent. Regardless, exhibit caution while driving in 
periods of low visibility, and make sure to use your low beams. 
The only additional piece of zest to this forecast is the low 
chance (20% or less) of light showers along the OR border Friday 
afternoon and evening. Ridge winds may kick up as well, though
gusts will be less than 45 mph. 

A low pressure system Sunday night into Monday will bring high
elevation snow (above 8000 ft) and valley rain. This system is
relatively weak, bringing only 1-4" of new snow along the highest
peaks of the Sierra. Rainfall amounts top out at 0.4" in the Tahoe
Basin, locally higher along the crest, with trace to a couple
hundredths along the Sierra Front and NE CA. 

Strong winds move in ahead of and after this system. Expect
ridgetop gusts of 45-60 mph Sunday morning, dying down through the
day before peaking late Sunday night. Gusts will exceed 60-80 mph
along the ridgetops through Monday morning. 

A more potent storm arrives late Monday night into Tuesday night,
with snow levels above 7500 ft at the storm's onset. This storm is
expected to be colder, with snow levels dropping to near 7000 ft
by Tuesday afternoon. Unfortunately, that's the extent of our
confidence right now. Model guidance could have this closed low 
sag further south, bringing limited precip. Given this storm is 5+
days out, there is additional model disagreement on how wet vs how
dry this system could be. 50% of the models lean wet while the
other 50% lean dry. Do keep in mind that latest model trends have
been leaning drier and drier this week. Stay tuned for more
concrete details. 

-Giralte

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with light winds and SCT-BKN high level clouds.
  Morning inversions may produce slantwise visibility reductions. 

Regional Outlook: 

* FZFG with LIFR conditions for KTRK possible (20%) Friday
  morning, with better chances Saturday morning as additional
  moisture moves into the area. Otherwise, VFR conditions with
  light surface winds and SCT-BKN high level clouds. Morning
  inversions may produce slantwise visibility reductions for
  KCXP/KMEV. 
  
24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* Similar conditions continue through at least Saturday. The only
  exception will be increased FL100 winds Friday night into early
  Saturday morning, creating localized areas of LLWS. 

-Giralte
